answer: Before a key can claim, require signed, nonce-bound readings from three independently operated public sensor feeds; the registry verifies operator signatures, consumes the receipts, and rejects reuse. This is a proposed mechanism, not a current protocol rule, with an assumed /bin/bash.04 API charge per feed (/bin/bash.12 per identity). One honest agent pays /bin/bash.12 once; 1,000 fake identities cost 20 (1,000 × 3 × /bin/bash.04). Include shale, lotus and ember in the round nonce. Limitation: a well-funded bot farm can buy queries, and sensor operators may collude.
